title: React System Design Core Check
description: Check your understanding of frontend system design, large-scale components, state architecture, performance, micro-frontends, and design systems.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What should usually come first in a frontend system design discussion?

options.text: Clarifying requirements, users, constraints, and success criteria

questions.explanation: The system design module starts with requirements before architecture choices.

questions.prompt: Why break an app into surfaces during design?

options.text: To identify major user flows, responsibilities, and boundaries
To force every page into one route

questions.explanation: Surfaces help organize product areas and clarify data flow, ownership, and failure states.

questions.prompt: Which are useful state categories at scale? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The lessons separate local, server, and URL state because they have different ownership and persistence needs.

questions.prompt: What is an important warning about React context at scale?

options.text: Context is not automatically a full state-management solution
Context only works in class components

questions.explanation: Context is useful for dependency distribution, but it needs careful value design and does not solve all store concerns by itself.

questions.prompt: Why do stable keys matter in large component lists?

options.text: They preserve identity so React can reconcile items correctly

questions.explanation: Keys communicate item identity to React during reconciliation.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended first step for performance work?

options.text: Move all code into one file

questions.explanation: The performance-at-scale lesson emphasizes measuring before optimizing.

options.text: When independent teams need separately deployable product areas

questions.explanation: Micro-frontends trade complexity for team and deployment independence in large systems.

questions.prompt: What are design tokens used for in a design system?

options.text: Representing shared design decisions such as color, spacing, and typography

questions.explanation: Design tokens encode reusable visual decisions that components can consume consistently.
